title: BCentral journal
description: Draft of 2026-10-28, batchId added 2026-10-29, point added 2026-11-16, register entries are contacts with an optional radio and the status chain is mesh-only since 2026-11-16. The data the app stores, exports and syncs to a hub. Entries are append-only and immutable; status is derived from status_change entries, never stored on the thing it describes. Every id is a ULID minted at creation, so objects can be created offline on any device and merged by union.

deviceId.description: The device this file or batch came from

publicKey.description: MeshCore node public key, 32 bytes as lowercase hex

clockTrust.description: How much the device's clock could be trusted when the timestamp was taken: synced over the network, set by hand by an operator, or neither

drill.description: True for an exercise (øvelse): every outgoing text of the incident is prefixed 'ØVELSE ' before '#n ' (text-protocol.md), and the incident is kept apart from real ones in lists and exports. Fixed at creation; absent means a real incident.

registerEntry.description: A person the staff talk to — a contact. Some have a radio (publicKey set); some are reached by phone, courier or in person. Binding a radio to a person is done by hand; nothing here is inferred. (Changed 2026-11-16: publicKey and origin optional.)

label.description: What the staff call them: a person's name, or 'radio #7' until handed out

phone.description: As typed; no format is enforced

origin.description: Of the radio, so only with a publicKey: issued = handed out per street by the association; adhoc = from the stack kept at the staff; private = bought by the person

journalEntry.description: Common envelope. The type decides which payload fields apply; the oneOf below enforces it.

deviceSeq.description: Per-device running number, gap-free. Lets a reader see whether anything is missing from one device's run.

operator.description: Who at the staff recorded this

counterpartyId.description: Register entry of the other end

seqNo.description: The #n of an outgoing message, per recipient per device; see text-protocol.md

batchId.description: Set on every message_out created by one send-to-all; the journal view groups them. Absent on a single send.

refersTo.description: Another entry (reply, status change, correction) or an incident (status change)

dedupeKey.description: Lowercase hex SHA-256 of '<sender public key hex>:<sender timestamp as decimal epoch seconds>:<text as received>'. Direct messages are encrypted to one companion, so no other device hears them; this key catches duplicate deliveries of the same message (a radio retry, a sync replay), not other devices' copies.

oneOf.description: message_out: staff → field. On transport mesh it is numbered per text-protocol.md (seqNo required, batchId allowed) and its status lives in status_change entries that refer to it. On any other transport it is a plain record of a message that went out by phone, courier or in person: no seqNo, no batchId, no status chain (changed 2026-11-16); follow-up is a point.
message_in: field → staff, stored as received. refersTo is set only by the operator by hand. dedupeKey is required for transport=mesh.
note: anything the operator writes into the journal that is not a message — a phone call made, a decision, an observation.

status_change: the only way status ever changes. refersTo is a mesh message_out (sent/delivered/roger/given_up, or closed = the staff stopped waiting for a confirmation; never a non-mesh one), an incident (closed/reopened) or a point (closed/reopened). A roger recorded from an incoming message also carries the incoming entry's id in text, or the operator's reason for a manual change.
correction: the entry refersTo was wrong; text says what is right. The original is never edited or removed.

point (da: punkt): something to follow up on, opened from a journal entry. refersTo is the entry it was opened from; text is its title. It is open from creation until a status_change closed refers to it, and open again after a status_change reopened. One entry can be the origin of at most one point; reopening uses the existing point.
